problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. Available containers are:
* Container 1: volume 2 cubic meters, revenue $256
* Container 2: volume 10 cubic meters, revenue $115
* Container 3: volume 22 cubic meters, revenue $36
* Container 4: volume 6 cubic meters, revenue $268
* Container 5: volume 34 cubic meters, revenue $140
* Container 6: volume 9 cubic meters, revenue $143
* Container 7: volume 22 cubic meters, revenue $227
* Container 8: volume 8 cubic meters, revenue $210
* Container 9: volume 45 cubic meters, revenue $12
* Container 10: volume 47 cubic meters, revenue $155
* Container 11: volume 36 cubic meters, revenue $163
* Container 12: volume 27 cubic meters, revenue $172
* Container 13: volume 32 cubic meters, revenue $167
* Container 14: volume 4 cubic meters, revenue $18
* Container 15: volume 32 cubic meters, revenue $75
* Container 16: volume 8 cubic meters, revenue $26
* Container 17: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue $138
* Container 18: volume 15 cubic meters, revenue $71
* Container 19: volume 41 cubic meters, revenue $275
* Container 20: volume 15 cubic meters, revenue $107
* Container 21: volume 33 cubic meters, revenue $161
* Container 22: volume 28 cubic meters, revenue $160
* Container 23: volume 30 cubic meters, revenue $254
* Container 24: volume 40 cubic meters, revenue $224
* Container 25: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue $114
* Container 26: volume 44 cubic meters, revenue $12
* Container 27: volume 46 cubic meters, revenue $120
* Container 28: volume 24 cubic meters, revenue $95

The vessel has a maximum cargo capacity of 481 cubic meters. Select the container combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container is either fully loaded or not loaded.
